create.name: Stephen Batchelor
create.bio:
Stephen Batchelor is a British writer and teacher who has spent half a century rethinking Buddhism for a secular age. He left England for Dharamsala at eighteen, took ordination as a Tibetan monk, and spent several years in Switzerland studying logic, philosophy and the Tibetan language under Geshe Rabten, translating Shantideva along the way. He then trained for four years in Korean Son with Kusan Sunim, where he met his wife Martine, before the couple joined the lay community at Sharpham in Devon and he turned to the Pali discourses.

His 1997 book Buddhism without Beliefs reached a wide readership among people drawn to practice but wary of doctrine, and was followed by Confession of a Buddhist Atheist, After Buddhism, Secular Buddhism, The Art of Solitude and, in 2025, Buddha, Socrates and Us, the last four from Yale. He co-founded Bodhi College, which teaches the early Buddhist texts to practitioners across Europe, and is a patron of Gaia House. Since the end of 2024 he has stepped back from leading courses to concentrate on writing and art at home in south-west France, though he still gives occasional talks and conversations online and in person.

books.title: Buddhism Without Beliefs: A Contemporary Guide to Awakening
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: His best-known book, a short guide to the dharma as a practice to be done rather than a set of beliefs to hold. It sets out the core teachings in plain language without relying on rebirth or other metaphysical claims.

books.title: Confession of a Buddhist Atheist
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: Part memoir, part reconstruction of the historical Buddha's life from the Pali texts, telling how his years as a Tibetan and Zen monk led him to a secular reading of the teaching.

books.title: After Buddhism: Rethinking the Dharma for a Secular Age
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: A close reading of the early discourses that argues for a dharma centred on tasks and ethical life, and places the Buddha's voice alongside those of several early disciples.

books.title: Secular Buddhism: Imagining the Dharma in an Uncertain World
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: A collection of essays written over three decades, tracing how his thinking moved from Tibetan and Zen training towards a secular, practice-led Buddhism.

books.title: The Art of Solitude
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: A meditation on being alone well, weaving Buddhist practice together with Montaigne, his own collage-making and long periods of retreat.

books.title: Buddha, Socrates, and Us: Ethical Living in Uncertain Times
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: His 2025 book, setting the Buddha beside Socrates to ask how ordinary people can live ethically when certainty is not on offer.

books.title: Living with the Devil: A Meditation on Good and Evil
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: An exploration of the figure of Mara in Buddhist stories and what it says about the forces in each of us that resist freedom, read alongside Western religious and literary sources.

books.title: Verses from the Center: A Buddhist Vision of the Sublime
books.author: Stephen Batchelor
books.description: His poetic translation of Nagarjuna's verses on the middle way, with an introduction that presents emptiness as an experience of awe rather than a dry philosophical position.
